slides.1.title: The Science of Oxidative Ageing in Tawny: Transformation in the Pipe
slides.1.html:
All of Tawny Port's appeal comes from the chemical transformation of long oxidative ageing in Pipes.

🪣 Pipe Specifications

  • The traditional Pipe holds about 550–630 litres (a small oak cask)
  • The small cask increases contact between wine and oak, speeding up oxidation
  • The wood is mainly Portuguese or American oak

🔄 Chemical Changes During Oxidative Ageing

  • Colour change: anthocyanins (deep red) → oxidative breakdown → amber-brown-orange, losing the red
  • Aroma evolution: fresh red fruit → dried fruit (raisin, fig) → nuts (almond, walnut) → caramel and toffee → coffee and chocolate (very old wines)
  • Evaporation: about 2–3% of the wine evaporates each year (the Angels' Share), further concentrating flavour
  • Sugar changes: some sugar continues to ferment during long cask ageing, slightly lowering sweetness

🌡️ The Maturation Environment of Gaia

  • Most Tawny is aged in Vila Nova de Gaia, across the river from Porto
  • The humid maritime environment slows evaporation and favours slow oxidation
  • Compared with natural ageing in the Douro Valley, Gaia's temperature is more stable
slides.2.title: 10 / 20 / 30 / 40 Year Tawny: What Is Really in the Bottle
slides.2.html:
The age statement on Tawny Port is one of the most easily misunderstood concepts in Portuguese wine.

📋 Age statement ≠ a specific harvest year

  • "20 Years Tawny" does not mean grapes harvested 20 years ago (in 2004)
  • It means that the "style age" of the blend of wines of different ages is about 20 years
  • The Blender mixes multi-vintage Tawnies of anywhere from 5 to 60 years old to ensure the finished wine shows the style of a "20-year" type

slides.3.question: What does a bottle of Port labelled "30 Years Tawny" mean?
slides.3.options.0: All the wine was harvested in a single year, 30 years ago (1994)
slides.3.options.1: The youngest wine in the blend is at least 30 years old
slides.3.options.2: A blend of wines of various ages that shows the complexity of a "style age of about 30 years"
slides.3.options.3: It is aged for a further 30 years in bottle before being sold
slides.3.explanation: The age statement on Tawny Port (10/20/30/40 years) represents the "style age" of the blend as a whole, not a specific harvest year. The blender mixes Tawnies of several different ages (perhaps 15–45 years) to ensure that colour, aroma and sweetness match the style of "30 Years".
slides.4.question: What is the main difference between Colheita and an ordinary "20 Years Tawny"?
slides.4.options.0: Colheita is a multi-vintage blend, 20 Years Tawny is a single vintage
slides.4.options.1: Colheita is a single-vintage Tawny (at least 7 years in cask, harvest year stated); 20 Years Tawny is a multi-vintage blend
slides.4.options.3: Colheita is made only from white grape varieties
slides.4.explanation: Colheita is the fine wine of the Tawny family: a single harvest year, aged at least 7 years in wood (usually longer), with the actual harvest year on the label. This gives Colheita both the oxidative complexity of Tawny and the vintage character of Vintage Port, making it the most refined type of Tawny.
